messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected — service=prefix-cache, region=us-west-2. p99 latency spike > 3s, streaming stalls observed. Alerts: paging oncall. Link: https://dash.redwood.example/alerts/3301234567

morgan: saw the alert at 10:02 PDT. p95 ~ 850ms -> 1.1s, p99 jumped to 3.6s. streaming tails > 5s for some requests. Low cache hit rate for v3-prefixhash keys (hitrate ~ 18%).

raj: I'm on it, grabbing dashboards. Any deploys in last 30m?

morgan: yes — rolled out prefix-hash v3 at 09:45 to us-west-2 only. Canary looked fine. Rollout reached 60% shortly before spike.

amy: confirming logs show increased cache misses and more backend paging to kv-store. Error rate for prefixcache misses -> backend read time increased p99 backend to 280ms.

elaine: customer support pinged — a small subset of high-throughput customers reported slow streaming responses. No 5xxs, but timeouts at customer side for streaming slice reads.

raj: okay, mitigation plan: 1) pause prefix-hash v3 rollout 2) re-enable salt v2 fallback for affected clusters 3) scale up prefetch workers to rehydrate hot prefixes 4) enable temporary routing to deduped cache nodes. Doing 1 now.

raj: /deployctl pause rollout prefix-hash:v3 --cluster us-west-2  (output: rollout paused @ 10:08)

ops-bot: Rollout paused by raj at 10:08. Canary remains active but new tokens not assigned to v3.

morgan: hitting the canary -> seems like hitrate for v2 slices jumps back to ~65% at 10:10 after pause. p99 trending down to 1.8s.

amy: starting prefetch scaling: 

```
kubectl scale deploy/prefetcher --replicas=12 -n inference-usw2
```

amy: prefetchers up (12 replicas) — backlog of rehydrate jobs processing hot prefixes.

raj: enabling salt v2 fallback routing in routing tier: /cfg apply routing.prefix_fallback=true zone=us-west-2

ops-bot: routing change applied by raj at 10:13.

morgan: after routing flip, streaming stall count dropped ~70% within 2 minutes. p99 now ~1.1s, p95 ~720ms. Still occasional tails for very large contexts (>8k tokens).

elaine: raised an incident ticket for affected customers, severity=high (customer visible latency, no data loss). Notifying CS and AMs.

raj: quick root-cause hypothesis: prefix-hash v3 altered salt mapping causing hot prefixes to remap across different kv-buckets; that caused cold misses and backend fanout -> paging. Canary missed the distribution skew.

amy: logs show evictions spiking around 09:58, eviction rate x3. KV read amplification increased. Also saw a small bug in prefetch key normalization in v3 which left some suffixes unmatched.

morgan: adding excerpts from logs: 

```
[09:58:12] prefixcache miss key=usr:embedding:abcd1234 remapped_to=kv-42 backend_read=142ms
[09:58:12] eviction: prefix=usr:embedding:abcd, reason=remap-hotshuffle
```

raj: next steps: 1) continue rollback of v3 to 0% 2) run targeted cache warmup for top N prefixes 3) create a temporary fallback routing rule for large-context streaming to use legacy cache path until warmup completes 4) postmortem owner and timeline.

morgan: I'll run the warmup job for top-500 prefixes: 

```
jobs/run_warmup --top 500 --cluster us-west-2 --async
```

morgan: warmup job queued at 10:18.

elaine: CS updated customers at 10:20: "We're aware of increased latency for streaming in us-west-2; mitigation in progress; next update in 30m."

ops-bot: Incident severity set to P1 by incident-bot at 10:21 — paging escalation to SRE rotation.

sre-oncall: I'm taking handoff from raj for oncall rotation in 15m. Assigning followups: warmup monitoring, postmortem draft, verify canary rollback completeness.

raj: handing off — summary: rolled back rollout pause -> currently at 0% v3. Routing fallback enabled. Prefetch scaled, warmup queued. Customer impact limited to a subset; no data loss. Logs and dashboards linked: https://dash.redwood.example/3301234567/graphs

sre-oncall: acknowledged. I'll monitor p95/p99 and streaming stall count. If p99 > 2s for >5m, re-escalate.

amy: note — need a follow-up codefix: prefetch key normalization bug in v3. Created GH PR: https://github.com/redwood/prefixcache/pull/472 (assigns: amy, raj).

morgan: current metrics at 10:30: p95=650ms, p99=1.05s, cache hitrate ~62% (us-west-2). Streaming stalls down to baseline. Looks stable so far.

elaine: CS: customers A and B were impacted intermittently. Recorded as "degraded streaming latency". Sending incident update to AMs.

sre-oncall: action items captured: [A] fix prefetch normalization (PR open), [B] postmortem + timeline (owner: raj), [C] add canary distribution test for mapping skew (owner: morgan), [D] run longer canary next rollout. I'll take A monitoring until we verify warmup fully completes.

raj: assigning postmortem, timeline and RCA. Will include steps to improve rollout checks and add synthetic hot-prefix tests.

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated at 10:34 (p99 < 1.2s sustained 10m), monitoring-only state.

morgan: leaving logs and notes in incident doc: https://docs.redwood.example/incidents/3301234567.

elaine: thank you team. I'll coordinate customer follow-ups. Update me if we see any regression when we re-rollout v3 after fixes. :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: closing handoff. Will post a short oncall notes message in #eng-sre after lunch.

amy: PR for fix is small, will request review. Plan to re-run canary with extended traffic sims after fix.

raj: postmortem owner and timeline set. Leaving the channel.

incident-bot: Incident closed by incident-bot at 10:42 — follow-ups remain.

(reacted with :white_check_mark: by morgan)"
